
TOPOLOGY
  processes       2 — every long-lived process this run starts, snug included:
                    snug        this process — resolves the policy and supervises
                    bwrap       the sandbox itself, and the payload inside it
                  No stage, no PRIVILEGED ancestor namespace — but see pid
                  nesting below: snug does create an unprivileged one.
  netns owner     sandbox
  pid nesting     depth 2 — snug forks bwrap into an intermediate user, pid AND
                  mount namespace of its own making, so bwrap is pid 1 THERE and
                  the sandbox's own pid namespace nests below it. A process left
                  at the intermediate level has no /proc entry inside the
                  sandbox: unaddressable, not merely unreadable.
                  snug re-execs itself there as `snug __inpidns`, which mounts a
                  procfs of that pid namespace over /proc and then EXECS the
                  bwrap below — still two processes. bwrap resolves its own
                  child's pid against that mount when it answers --info-fd; on
                  the host's it reads a stranger, or nothing at all.
                  That mount is why the intermediate user namespace maps this
                  uid to root INSIDE it. It is a rootless root: it reaches one
                  host uid, yours, and bwrap maps the payload back down — the
                  payload's own uid, gid and capability sets are unchanged.
                  Cost: one more of the kernel's 32 user-namespace nesting
                  levels, and this run needs at least 2 each of
                  /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces and max_pid_namespaces.
  subuid          none (one uid, mapped by the intermediate user namespace snug creates:
                  no /etc/subuid line, no newuidmap/newgidmap, no setuid binary
                  on this path)
  control         none — there is no stage to control.
